metadata.title: Stacks Processes and Sockets
metadata.subject: NCC — Net-Centric Computing
metadata.contentType: Original practice based on the accompanying lecture notes

questions.question: A mail relay accepts a message and forwards it to another mail server. What happens to the transport connection?
options: A) The original TCP segment continues unchanged through the relay
B) The relay uses a separate TCP connection for the next transfer
C) The original client socket moves into the next server
D) DNS extends the original connection without another handshake
questions.explanation: A relay terminates an application transaction and originates another; TCP state belongs to each connection.

questions.question: Which boundary does the socket API expose to a typical network application?
options: A) A direct interface to the remote Ethernet switch table
B) The physical radio modulation of every transmitted bit
C) The local interface used to request transport communication
D) A mailbox address that replaces the destination port
questions.explanation: The process uses a local socket API while the operating system normally handles TCP and IP.

questions.question: What is the correct interpretation of a successful application write to a TCP socket?
options: A) The receiving SMTP server has accepted the email
B) The local system has accepted bytes for transmission
C) The destination mailbox has stored the message
D) The recipient has read the message
questions.explanation: A local write can return before remote transport receipt or application acceptance.

questions.question: Which statement correctly maps Internet functions to OSI concepts?
options: A) MIME requires a separate presentation-layer packet on every link
B) TCP is classified as the OSI session protocol because it has connections
C) Representation and session functions can be implemented within Internet application functionality
D) DNS becomes a network-layer protocol because applications depend on it
questions.explanation: OSI functions need not correspond to separate Internet implementation modules or headers.

questions.question: In a common desktop mail configuration, what does the mail application contact first?
options: A) Every recipient domain authoritative DNS server directly
B) The recipient laptop Ethernet interface
C) The final mailbox using an SMTP connection from every browser
D) Its configured message submission service
questions.explanation: A configured submission service handles outgoing mail; later MTA relay can use recipient MX records.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes encapsulation for plaintext SMTP over Ethernet?
options: A) SMTP bytes inside Ethernet inside TCP inside IP
B) SMTP bytes inside DNS inside ARP inside TCP
C) SMTP bytes inside TCP inside IP inside Ethernet
D) SMTP bytes inside TCP inside Ethernet inside IP
questions.explanation: Each lower layer carries the higher-layer data in its payload.

questions.question: A TCP server accepts several clients on port 25. How can it distinguish their established connections?
options: A) By their source and destination IP addresses and ports
B) By the server port alone
C) By requiring every connection to use a different server port
D) By the visible To message header
questions.explanation: Accepted connections have distinct connection tuples even when the local listening port is shared.

questions.question: What is the role of the listening socket after accept produces a connected socket?
options: A) It must become the connected client socket and stop listening
B) It is converted into a DNS resolver
C) It can continue accepting additional connections
D) It stores the recipient message body
questions.explanation: Listening and connected sockets serve different roles in a typical TCP server.

questions.question: Which identifier is used for local delivery of a frame to a link interface?
options: A) The SMTP subject
B) A TCP receive window
C) A DNS MX preference
D) A MAC address
questions.explanation: MAC addresses identify link interfaces within the relevant link or bridged LAN.

questions.question: Why can a TCP read return only part of one SMTP command?
options: A) TCP always removes the first half of a command
B) An SMTP command is required to use exactly two packets
C) The Ethernet switch chooses where a command ends
D) TCP provides a byte stream without preserving application write boundaries
questions.explanation: SMTP must parse its own CRLF framing after TCP reconstructs stream bytes.

questions.question: Where is TLS normally placed relative to plaintext SMTP and TCP?
options: A) Below Ethernet and above physical signals
B) Above TCP and below application plaintext
C) Inside the IPv4 TTL field
D) In place of both DNS and TCP
questions.explanation: TLS protects application communication carried by the TCP stream; it does not replace IP or link delivery.

source.section: Section 2 — OSI and TCP IP models

questions.question: Which fields form the five-tuple commonly used to identify a transport flow?
options: A) Source IP, destination IP, source port, destination port, transport protocol
B) Sender mailbox, recipient mailbox, subject, date, message ID
C) Source MAC, destination MAC, TTL, window, DNS preference
D) Source IP, destination IP, source MAC, destination MAC, SMTP command
questions.explanation: The TCP four-tuple plus protocol distinguishes flows at the network and transport boundary.

questions.question: How does the four-layer TCP/IP model differ from the five-layer Internet teaching model?
options: A) It removes transport and puts TCP directly into SMTP
B) It groups link and physical functions into one network-access or link layer
C) It adds an independent MIME layer
D) It classifies IP as an application protocol
questions.explanation: The grouping differs while the actual data-delivery functions remain.

questions.question: A user sends email in a web browser. Which initial network protocol is typical?
options: A) SMTP directly from every browser to the recipient MX
B) ARP across the Internet to the recipient mailbox
C) IMAP from the browser to every destination router
D) HTTPS between the browser and webmail provider
questions.explanation: A webmail backend can originate SMTP after receiving the browser request.

questions.question: What does an ephemeral source port identify in the example A:49152 to B:25?
options: A) The client transport endpoint for that connection
B) The client Ethernet switch port number
C) The recipient mailbox local part
D) The MX priority of the recipient server
questions.explanation: The operating system selects a local ephemeral transport port; it is separate from MAC and mailbox addressing.

questions.question: Which two events can be absent from a successful capture because relevant information is cached?
options: A) DNS resolution exchanges and ARP exchanges
B) TCP data delivery and all physical signaling
C) The destination IP address and transport port
D) All SMTP replies and the receiving process
questions.explanation: Caches can eliminate supporting lookups, while the actual communication still uses the corresponding addressing information.
